name: Tattenai
title: Governor of the province beyond the River
summary: Tattenai was the Persian governor over the province beyond the River (Trans-Euphrates) at the time when the Jews were rebuilding the temple in Jerusalem after the exile. He questioned the Jews' right to build the temple and sent a report to King Darius, who then confirmed Cyrus's original decree and gave permission to complete the construction. Tattenai thus played an indirect but important role in the rebuilding of God's temple.

keyEvents.title: Tattenai investigates the temple construction
keyEvents.description: Tattenai, the governor beyond the River, and his associate Shetar-Bosnai came to Jerusalem and asked the Jews who had given them permission to rebuild the temple and finish the walls.

keyEvents.title: The Jews' answer to Tattenai
keyEvents.description: The Jewish elders explained that they had received permission from King Cyrus of Persia to rebuild God's house, and they gave the names of the leaders responsible for the construction.

keyEvents.title: Tattenai sends a letter to King Darius
keyEvents.description: Tattenai wrote a detailed letter to King Darius reporting on the temple construction and asking the king to check the royal archives to see if there was indeed an authorization from Cyrus.

keyEvents.title: King Darius Finds Cyrus's Decree
keyEvents.description: King Darius ordered that an investigation be made in the archives, and Cyrus's original decree was found in Ecbatana, confirming the permission to rebuild the temple in Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Tattenai Ordered to Support the Construction
keyEvents.description: King Darius commanded Tattenai and Shethar-Bozenai to stay away from the work and not hinder the rebuilding. They were also instructed to support the Jews with funds from the province's tax revenues.

keyEvents.title: Tattenai Obeys the King's Command
keyEvents.description: Tattenai and his associates followed King Darius's command exactly, and the temple was completed with their support. This led to the dedication of God's house with great joy.
